title: Mahatma Gandhi
examples: What was the main goal of the Salt March?
How did non-violence help the Indian independence movement?
Can you explain what the British salt tax was?

explain.say: Today we learn about Mahatma Gandhi's important life work. He taught people to protest without using any violence.
A key part of his protest was the Salt March. This march was a very famous event.
The British government taxed salt very heavily. This tax made life very difficult for poor people.
The movement aimed for India's independence from British rule. This was a huge national goal.
In everyday life, we see non-violence when we protest for better schools. We can march peacefully to show our voices.
A common mistake is thinking protest means shouting loudly all the time. You must keep your message calm and clear.

faq.q: What exactly was the Salt March about?
faq.a: The Salt March was a protest against the unfair British tax on salt. Gandhi led people to make salt themselves.
asks: Why did they march to the sea?
What was the purpose of the salt tax protest?

faq.q: How did non-violence work as a protest method?
faq.a: Non-violence meant resisting injustice without fighting or harming anyone. It showed the moral strength of the people.
asks: What is the power of peaceful protest?

faq.q: What did the British tax on salt do?
faq.a: The tax made a basic necessity very expensive for everyone. It was seen as an unfair control by the rulers.
asks: Why was salt important to the people?
What was the impact of the salt tax?

faq.q: What was the main goal of Gandhi's actions?
faq.a: His main goal was to achieve full independence for India. He worked for the rights of all Indians.
asks: Was he fighting for a specific group?
What did he want for India?

faq.q: When did the movement for independence happen?
faq.a: The movement was a long process that built up over many years. It finally led to India gaining freedom in 1947.
asks: What marked the end of British rule?

facts: Mahatma Gandhi was a leader in the Indian independence movement.
The Salt March began in 1930 as a protest against the salt tax.
Non-violent protest relies on moral courage rather than force.
The goal of the movement was to achieve self-rule for India.

quiz.why: Non-violence kept the focus on the injustice, not on fighting.

wrong.0: The British reacted to the protest's message, not just the method.

quiz.say: If a country taxed salt heavily, the best non-violent response is:

options.show: Start a physical fight at the tax office.
options.say: Start a physical fight at the tax office.

options.say: Pay the tax and complain privately.
